cues.caption: Live replay: a real ShanghaiT2DM patient, scored by a model trained without them
The clock starts 75 minutes before this period's first low; only records up to the clock are used
Each step adds the next readings and recomputes the forecasts with the evaluation's code
08:22: the reading is 79.5 mg/dL, just above this fold's 79 threshold, so no alert
08:37: 67 mg/dL. The low began without a warning, so the evaluation counts it as missed
Jump to 75 minutes before a night-time low in the same period: 02:37, reading 79.5
02:52 at night: 76 mg/dL is at or below 79, so the rule alerts. The forecasts expected a rise
Revealed for scoring only, never given to the model: the reading kept falling
The low began at 03:52, so the evaluation scored this alert as matched, 60 minutes ahead
Parity: the live forecast equals the evaluation's stored prediction for this moment
03:52: the low has begun. No repeat alert during the low or within the 60-minute cooldown
Sensor dropout: with the last 45 minutes missing, the twin says unavailable instead of guessing
A synthetic GLP-1 start fires the dose-review rule; it does not refit the physiology
Reset: the clock returns to the end of the 5-day calibration; nothing carries over
Clinic list (synthetic patients): review triggers and safety notes, judged as of the demo date
Meena (synthetic): medicines and dated records; each trigger shows its reason and label note
Dose scenarios: options side by side on her core, under stated assumptions (illustrative)
More process noise: the ranking holds, but the percentages move with the assumption
Evidence: retrospective results against baselines, including the negative findings
Example record shapes: a FHIR-style bundle and smartwatch data (display only, not validated)
